card.title: Russian
card.text: From the Cyrillic alphabet to C1, with the grammar explained and stress marks shown throughout.

heading: Learn Russian with the grammar explained.
lead: A complete Russian course for English speakers, from reading Cyrillic to C1: 78 modules in eight tiers. The cases, verbal aspect and verbs of motion are taught directly, with stress marks shown throughout, and every exercise tells you why an answer is right or wrong.
fineprint: The whole course is free. Specialization courses, TORFL practice papers, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

panel.label: The course, tier by tier

items.title: First words and sentences
items.text: Greetings, gender, pronouns, the present tense, numbers.

items.title: Cases and the past
items.text: Plurals, the prepositional and accusative cases, the past tense.

items.title: Everyday life
items.text: The genitive, dative and instrumental, the future, verbs of motion.

items.title: Building fluency
items.text: Plural cases, aspect, the imperative, comparatives.

items.title: Intermediate
items.text: Prefixed motion verbs, the conditional, complex sentences.

items.title: Upper intermediate
items.text: Participles, verbal adverbs, word formation, reported speech.

items.title: Advanced
items.text: Fine points of aspect and motion, style, registers, idioms.

panel.note: 78 modules. The last tiers also cover topics such as law, the media, science, medicine, history and literature.

sections.heading: What the course teaches, and how

items.title: Cyrillic first
items.text: The first tier teaches the alphabet and its sounds, all 33 letters, word stress and the main sound rules, before any grammar.

items.title: Stress marks throughout
items.text: Russian spelling does not show stress, so the course marks it throughout, as in ру́сский язы́к. Reading and listening texts come with audio.

items.title: The grammar taught directly
items.text: All six cases, verbal aspect, verbs of motion with and without prefixes, participles and verbal adverbs each have their own modules, explained in plain English with examples.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer gets feedback with a reason and a link to the grammar rule behind it. Every Russian word can be tapped for its meaning, its forms and audio.

items.title: Pronunciation feedback
items.text: Russian has pronunciation assessment, so the course's speaking exercises give feedback on how you pronounce what you say.

items.title: A placement test
items.text: If you already know some Russian, the placement test shows where to start, so you do not have to work through what you know.

sections.heading: Practice papers for TORFL
sections.intro: The course has timed practice papers for the TORFL (ТРКИ), the Russian state test of Russian as a foreign language, at five levels, two papers each. They cover vocabulary and grammar, reading, listening and writing; the papers have no speaking subtest. What the papers cover and how they differ from the real test.

sections.heading: Russian for your field
sections.intro: Thirteen specialization courses, nine modules each, in three stages: Foundations, written for learners at Tier 4 of the core course, Working vocabulary for Tier 6 and Professional for Tier 8. Each teaches the vocabulary and register of one field.

items.question: Is the Russian course really free?
items.answer: Yes. All 78 modules from the alphabet to C1, the grammar reference, word practice, the placement test and 5 Ask AI questions a day are free. Premium adds the specializations, TORFL papers, conversation practice, stories and the other extras.

items.question: Do I need to know the Cyrillic alphabet first?
items.answer: No. The first tier teaches it from the start: all 33 letters, word stress and the main sound rules.

items.question: How does it handle the cases and verbs of motion?
items.answer: The cases are taught one at a time and then again in the plural, and verbs of motion are taught over four modules, from идти́ and ходи́ть to prefixed and figurative uses. The rules are explained, not left to be guessed from examples.

items.question: Will it get me through TORFL?
items.answer: It cannot promise that. The TORFL papers practise the test's task formats at five levels and show your share of points, but they are shorter than the real subtests and have no speaking part. The course behind them teaches what a paper shows you are missing.

items.question: What level does the course reach?
items.answer: C1. The last tier covers the fine points of aspect, figurative verbs of motion, word order, particles, registers and style, colloquial Russian and idioms.

closing.heading: Start with the alphabet, or wherever you are.
closing.text: Sign in with Google, take the placement test if you already know some Russian, and open the first module.
